importance_ranking.reason: Tin sheds vary significantly in visual form — roof shape (sloping vs flat vs pyramid), colour, frame type, and scale (residential terrace cover vs large industrial shed) are all immediately readable from a photo. Buyers scan images first to confirm the structure type matches their requirement before reading any text.

Sheet thickness, coating type, and span/height are primary shortlisting criteria — a buyer needing a 0.50 mm colour-coated industrial shed cannot substitute a 0.35 mm bare GI residential shed. Listings without these specs cannot be evaluated for project fit.

Per-sq-ft pricing varies substantially with sheet thickness, coating type, and insulation — buyers compare rates across sellers only after confirming spec equivalence. Indian B2B buyers in construction and fabrication are highly price-aggressive and use listed per-sq-ft rates as the primary comparison lever.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Some sellers quote per kg (sheet-only supply) or lump-sum per project (large PEB sheds) — unit must be shown alongside price to prevent miscomparison. Per sq ft is the dominant and expected unit for complete supply-and-install transactions.
importance_ranking.reason: Price cannot be compared across listings without knowing whether the quote is per sq ft of covered area, per kg of sheet material, or a lump-sum project price. Unit ambiguity is a real and common market problem in this category.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: No dominant fabricator brand with buyer recall exists — buyers search by spec, span, and price; the raw material brands (Jindal, JSW, TATA, APL Apollo) are steel suppliers, not shed fabricators that buyers search for by name.
importance_ranking.reason: Buyers evaluate fabricator credibility (past project photos, service area, installation capability) after spec and price shortlisting — especially for large industrial or warehouse sheds where post-sale erection quality matters.

top_configurator_specs.reason: Coating type (Bare GI vs Colour Coated vs Aluminium Zinc) defines the product tier and drives the largest per-sq-ft price delta — Galvalume/AZ-coated sheds command a significant premium over bare GI, and colour-coated PPGI sits between them; values are non-interchangeable across buyer requirements.

Thickness (0.30 mm to 0.50 mm) is the primary structural and durability differentiator within each coating tier — thicker sheets command higher per-sq-ft rates and are non-substitutable for industrial vs residential applications.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Buyers universally search and quote by span (12 ft, 20 ft, 30 ft, 50 ft+) — span determines the structural frame design, purlin spacing, and total material cost, making it the primary project-sizing spec that sellers need to price accurately.

Insulated variants (PUF sandwich panel, EPS core) command a substantially higher per-sq-ft rate than uninsulated GI sheds and serve a distinct buyer segment (heat-sensitive industrial applications) — sellers need this to confirm product fit and price correctly.

top_rfq_specs.reason: Colour is the primary visual differentiator that sellers need to confirm material availability and quote accurately — each colour corresponds to a specific PPGI/PPGL coil stock that may or may not be in the fabricator's inventory.
Height (eave height or ridge height) determines the structural frame design and total material quantity — sellers need this to assess fabrication complexity and provide an accurate per-sq-ft quote.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Sellers cannot determine frame design, purlin count, or material cost without knowing the required span — it is the single most important project-sizing dimension buyers specify when requesting a tin shed quote.
